title: Computer audio: record the output the call plays to, not only the default output
description: Loopback records the default console output. Call apps often play to the default communications output (a headset), so the other side was recorded as silence. description: At a call start meetwatch sees which capture device the call app has open (for example a virtual noise-removal mic). The meeting recording should take that device, not the dictation mic setting, when the setting's device is silent or differs. Settings keeps a way to force one.
close_reason: Meeting page: two small meters in the Stop row (look C, picked by the owner), device and state on hover, a warning with a one-click switch when a source is silent and the call app uses another device; the worker follows the call's mic and output by itself after 20 s of silence. The meeting page (and the chip on hover) shows the mic and the output device being recorded, a live level bar for each, and when a source stays silent while the call app uses a different device (meetwatch already knows the call app's mic), a plain warning with a one-click switch. title: Open Ecoscribe opens no window when a browser tab is titled Ecoscribe
description: The tray's Open Ecoscribe looks for a window titled Ecoscribe and only focuses it. On Windows 11 a browser tab with that title gets an Explorer stand-in window (Windows.Internal.Shell.TabProxyWindow) with the same title, and the tests' quiet window copies are hidden windows with that title too. Either one is taken for the app's window, so nothing opens. Fix: only a visible pywebview window (WindowsForms class) counts.
close_reason: Open Ecoscribe now only takes a visible pywebview window for the app's own; a browser tab's Explorer stand-in and hidden test copies are skipped. New unit tests; checked on the desktop: the old lookup picked the tab stand-in, the new one the real window.

title: Real call detection check on macOS
description: Actual Teams/Slack/Zoom/Meet/FaceTime/Signal calls raise the prompt and stop after the call. Needs the user on a call. Was uat.9/13.
notes:
2026-10-22: the user tried a real call on the Mac a few days ago (build before #128): no prompt when the call started and nothing when it ended. #128 (merged 2026-10-22) changes browser-call detection to two-way audio and joins a hand-started meeting to the call; it is untested on a real call. Next on the Mac: build a .dmg from main, find out which app the failed call used (from the user, not from logs in git), reproduce with detect_log / ecoscribe.log, fix, then the user rechecks on a real call.
2026-10-22 (branch mac-call-detect): code fixes without a Mac. Each Core Audio audio process now counts as the app responsible for it (then bundle id, then the .app path): WebKit views inside call apps, unknown helper bundles (Arc), FaceTime's avconferenced daemon were misnamed or missed. A browser talks if any of its processes plays sound. Arc/Vivaldi/Chromium added. One failing reader (window titles without Accessibility) no longer fails the whole meetwatch tick. detect.log now has 'signal' lines (apps on the mic, +sound, title yes/no, accessibility / process-list problems) and 'tick failed'. Mac session must: (1) run python -m ecoscribe.callprobe --raw during a real call in each app the user uses (Meet in Chrome/Safari/Arc, Zoom, Teams, Slack huddle, FaceTime) and check each shows '-> a call' and 'would now offer to record', then the end after hanging up; (2) build a .dmg from main, do one real call, read the signal lines in detect.log; if accessibility=not-granted shows, re-grant Accessibility for the new build. Keep open until a real call prompts and ends on the Mac.

title: Browser practice pages that use the mic and play sound are taken for calls
description: Why: since Windows reads audio sessions (1.23.1), a browser on the mic that also plays sound counts as a call. A local language-practice or voice page does exactly that, so the meeting prompt pops up on every turn. What: [meetings] not_calls, a list of words; a browser window whose title has one of them doesn't count as a call by mic + sound alone (a meeting tab title still does). Empty by default.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: a browser talking with a not_calls title open is not a call; a meeting title still starts one; empty list changes nothing.
close_reason: Shipped in 1.24.1: [meetings] not_calls; unit tests cover the rule, installed through the release gate, set locally and checked that the practice page's window title matches.

title: Windows: calls go undetected when Windows stops recording mic use
description: The call detector on Windows reads only the consent store (CapabilityAccessManager LastUsedTimeStart/Stop). On the owner's PC that record stopped updating after a restart: an app capturing the mic (a browser call, a test recorder) left no entry, so no call was detected while the Windows audio sessions showed the browser actively capturing the headset. Fix: also read the active audio sessions on capture devices (and, for browsers, an active session on an output device as two-way audio, like macOS).
acceptance_criteria: A process with an active capture session counts as on the mic even when the consent store has nothing; a browser that also has an active output session counts as talking; tests cover the merge; real check on the PC during a browser call.
notes: Merged in #202, released and installed as 1.23.1. Checked live on the PC before the install: during a browser call the new reader reported the browser on the mic and playing sound (a call) while the consent store showed nothing. Left: the installed 1.23.1 catching a real call on its own (detect.log shows a 'signal mic=<app>' line and the Take notes box appears); close then.
close_reason: Released in 1.23.1 (#202). The installed app caught a real browser call by itself: detect.log shows the start, the Take notes box and a browser on the mic playing sound, while Windows' consent store still recorded nothing.

title: Move the pill: drag the meeting chip, it stays where it was put
description: The user wants to move the pill out of the way. Drag the meeting chip with the mouse; the pill (meeting chip and dictation pill) then shows at that spot, remembered across restarts; double-click puts it back at the bottom centre. The chip stops being click-through only while the mouse is on it, so a press there doesn't reach the app below.
close_reason: Drag the meeting chip to move the pill; the spot is kept in pill.json and the dictation pill shows there too; double-click puts it back; click-through except while the mouse is on the chip. Unit tests for the drag logic, Win32 calls probed on the PC; a live drag try after install.

title: GPU tests: test workers must not run the user's after_transcribe command
description: Tests that start a real --transcribe worker read the user's config.toml. With [transcribe] after_transcribe set, the user's own program runs on the test's session folder and changes it, so test_worker_cli_exits_and_frees_vram and test_greek_spanish_mixed_file fail although the transcription itself is fine. Windows fix: conftest gives the run a copy of config.toml without that key. macOS keeps config and models in one folder (ECOSCRIBE_DATA_DIR), so it needs its own way: done, ticket, or not needed.
close_reason: conftest gives the test run a copy of config.toml without after_transcribe (Windows); test_worker_cli_exits_and_frees_vram passes again; unit suite 890 passed

title: Old NVIDIA driver: dictation fails instead of running on the CPU, and nobody is told
description: Seen on a colleague's PC: the NVIDIA driver is older than the CUDA 12 runtime Ecoscribe ships. Every engine worker tries CUDA, fails ('driver version is insufficient'), falls back to small/cpu in the same process, and then dies or never becomes ready, so dictation fails twice and is lost. status.json keeps saying device=cuda with no fallback (on-demand mode writes it once at start), so the window and debug info hide it. Separately, the freeze watchdog reported 40-minute and 3-hour freezes overnight that were the PC asleep.
acceptance_criteria: A worker whose CUDA load fails records why and exits; the next worker goes straight to the CPU (no CUDA attempt, no same-process fallback) for this app run. status.json shows device=cpu and the reason once known. A too-old driver gets a plain notice to update it. CPU dictations get a longer reply timeout. The app logs a dead worker's exit code; the worker writes native crashes to the crash folder. The freeze watchdog ignores time the PC was asleep. Tests cover each.
close_reason: Worker notes a GPU failure and exits; later workers start on the CPU until the app or driver changes; status and a plain notice say so; longer CPU timeouts; worker exit codes and native crashes logged; freeze watch ignores sleep; debug info shows the GPU and driver.

description: A meeting's speakers pass is held until no meeting is recording, so on a day of back-to-back calls it waits for hours and the window says 'identifying speakers...' the whole time. The GPU has room for it next to live transcription. Run speakers jobs while a meeting records when the GPU has enough free memory; otherwise wait, and show an honest 'waiting' label instead of 'identifying speakers...'.

title: Google Calendar sign-in: meeting names and guests (Email participants) without the secret iCal link
description: Some Google Workspace accounts have the secret iCal address turned off by the admin, so meetings get no name or guests and Email participants opens with an empty To. Add Settings > Meetings > Connect Google Calendar: a one-time sign-in in the browser (OAuth for desktop apps: loopback redirect + PKCE, read-only scope calendar.events.readonly). The background app then reads today's events like the iCal feed (title, guests' names and addresses, Meet link), picks the event of a call by time and Meet link, and Email participants on an older meeting looks up the event at its start time. The refresh token is kept on this computer only (DPAPI-encrypted on Windows). Needs an OAuth client of type Desktop app from a Google Cloud project, placed as google_client.json in the data folder.

title: Speech coaching: help the user speak more clearly from how they dictate
description: The user wants to improve how they speak using their dictation history. Research basis: ASR confidence correlates with intelligibility; immediate feedback reduces filler words without raising anxiety; hedges and hesitations lower perceived confidence; comprehension peaks around 130-160 wpm. Caveat: most dictation is thinking aloud to an AI, so coaching focuses on dictations to people (messages, email) and later the user's side of meetings. Everything computed locally; nothing personal ever goes in git (tests use invented text).
